lines.text: A small port of traders and pearl divers that grew rich on oil, was overrun by its neighbour, and rose again. This is the story of Kuwait.
Some four thousand years ago, Failaka Island, off the coast, was already a trading post. Later, Greeks would leave their mark there too.
In the 1750s a town grew on the shore of the bay, a walled port of merchants, ship builders and pearl divers.
Soon the Al-Sabah family came to rule it, and they have ruled Kuwait ever since.
In 1895 Abdullah Al-Salim was born, the emir who would one day lead his country to independence.
In 1899, wary of its powerful neighbours, Kuwait signed a treaty that made it a British protectorate.
Jaber Al-Ahmad, born in 1926, would be emir in Kuwait's darkest hour, and see it freed.
In 1938 oil was struck at Burgan. It proved one of the largest fields in the world, and it changed everything.
Mishal Al-Ahmad, born in 1940, would become emir in 2023.
In 1953 Kuwait began saving its oil wealth for the future, in what became the world's oldest sovereign wealth fund.
Independence came in 1961, and the next year a constitution set up the first elected parliament in the Gulf.
By the late seventies, three slender towers rose over the bay, the Kuwait Towers, a symbol of the modern country.
In 1980 the state brought its oil business together in one national company.
Two years later an unofficial stock market crashed, leaving debts of some ninety-four billion dollars.
In 1986 the Grand Mosque opened, the largest in the country.
Then, in 1990, came the crisis that would define a generation, and a war to undo it.
In August 1990 Iraqi forces poured across the border and occupied Kuwait.
Early in 1991 a coalition led by the United States drove them out, and Kuwait was free again.
But as they fled, Iraqi troops set hundreds of oil wells ablaze, and black smoke filled the sky for months.
In 2005 Kuwaiti women won the right to vote.
And in 2019 a causeway named after Sheikh Jaber opened across the bay, one of the longest sea bridges in the world.
From pearl boats to oil wealth and liberation, Kuwait's story is one of a small nation that endured.
